newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai revenue rises 11.8 pct in fiscal 1996.
newsitem.headline: Thai revenue rises 11.8 pct in fiscal 1996.

text.p: Thailand said on Monday that government revenue in fiscal 1996 ended September 30, 1996, rose 11.8 percent over the previous fiscal year.
Revenues in the fiscal year just ended rose to 850.18 billion baht ($34 billion) from 760.14 billion baht in the previous year, the finance ministry said in a statement.
Government spending in fiscal 1996 amounted to 777.25 billion baht against 670.55 billion baht in the previous year, it added.
Tax collection by the revenue department totalled 507.99 billion baht compared with 444.15 billion baht in the previous fiscal period, the statement said.
The excise department's revenue from October 1995 to September 1996 totalled 167.16 billion baht against 155.31 billion baht in the previous corresponding period, it said.
The government's outstanding debts at the end of September totalled 701.34 billion baht, it said.
The ministry did not give the amount of outstanding debt at the end of September last year.
Of the government's total debt, 331.98 billion baht was borrowings from domestic sources, while the remaining 369.36 billion baht was borrowed from abroad, it said.
